item.title: Atomic File Replacement on NTFS Is Not rename + fsync
item.description: shipmates writes a lot of small state files that other processes read. Voyage plans and state, tracker files. Each of them has to be replaced atomically, so a reader sees the old file or the new one and never half of each. Each also has to be replaced durably. When the function returns success, a power cut doesn’t take it back. Every Unix programmer knows the recipe for that. It doesn’t work on Windows, and the reasons are more interesting than “Windows is different”.
